newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - FTSE may ease to 4,625 after slow start.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - FTSE may ease to 4,625 after slow start.

text.p: The FTSE 100 index will be unable to move too far in either direction at the start of trading on Friday which will frustrate market bulls and bears, technical analyst said.
But a slightly negative bias may begin to appear as the day wears on which may take the FTSE down to about 4,625, they added. By 0725 GMT, the FTSE was indicated down 3.4 at 4,654.5.

A daily bar chart of the index over the past week shows the current struggle the market has been having in recouping its losses from mid-June with investor restlessness manifesting itself by bouts of frenzied activity and changes of direction.
By Thursday, the FTSE had almost made a 50 percent retracement of the fall to Tuesday's intra-day low of 4,538 from a high of 4,796 on June 13.
But it also hit a barrier in the form of its 10 day moving average and the danger now is for the current churning action to take the market lower, analysts said.

Not will concern about the July 2 budget concentrate the minds of investors but the fumbling on Wall Street will also give reasons to investors not participate too heavily in the market -- giving way to thin trading conditions and opening the possibilty of sharp price movements.

A daily bar chart of the Dow over the past week indicates lower intra-day highs and although there appears to be immediate chart support at 7,490, it does look suspect and this will not help sentiment in London, analysts said.
On Thursday, the Dow Jones industrials closed down 35.73 at 7,654.25.
